result.title: Loss Curvature as a Sampling-Free Proxy for Memorization in Diffusion Models
result.summary: Understanding the mechanism behind why diffusion models memorize their training data remains an open question in generative modeling. In this paper, we examine this question from two perspectives: (a) the model-level perspective concerning the onset of memorization in a model during training, and (b) the sample-level perspective concerning the proclivity of an individual sample to be memorized by a given model. We show that the so-called input loss curvature, or the Frobenius norm of the Hessian of the diffusion model's training loss, is an effective metric for quantifying both perspectives on memorization. In particular, we empirically demonstrate that input curvatures averaged across training and validation samples can identify when a model is likely to start regurgitating its training data when tracked over training time. However, this metric is not sufficient for measuring an individual sample's likelihood of being memorized. To address this perspective, we introduce a counterfactual definition of memorization in diffusion models, extending the analogous notion from supervised learning proposed by [Feldman, 2019]. We prove that this counterfactual memorization is controlled by the input curvature of the leave-one-out model, thus establishing a direct theoretical link between a sample's local loss landscape and its generation likelihood. We validate our derived bounds through several empirical experiments and show that input-dependent curvature provides a proxy for memorization.

AI.brief_summary: 论文从模型层面与样本层面考察扩散模型为何记忆训练数据，提出用训练损失 Hessian 的 Frobenius 范数（输入损失曲率）作为免采样的记忆度量：训练/验证样本的平均曲率可指示记忆起始时刻，并引入反事实记忆定义，证明其受留一模型曲率控制，再用实验验证该界。
AI.relevance_reason: Hessian 曲率与留一（leave-one-out）影响量构成的免采样样本级归因线索，可能可供核查迁移到 VLM 推理轨迹训练中的贡献分配与监督评估；但原文面向图像扩散的记忆机制，与视觉 latent 推理无直接关联。
